leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single prize part for B025 naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, with citations that differ only in wording (physiology of GLP-1 and identification of its active form, enabling incretin-based therapies). Linnarsson moved from his opening trio (Drucker, Holst, Knudsen) to Mojsov after reading colleagues, so the six now agree on names as well as on the ballot ID. What is shared: a mature, replicated mechanism and a large clinical consequence. What is not settled: every member records the same reservations, namely the contested priority for the active peptide, Habener's absence from the credited names, and the exclusion of Knudsen. Linnarsson says he would move toward Knudsen only if the committee decides the citation should explicitly reward the therapeutic step, and Wahren-Herlenius names Knudsen as the first name to revisit for a therapeutic arm.

areas_of_agreement: All six members explicitly prefer B025 as the whole of their round-1 configuration, with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov as laureates.
Members agree B025 is mature: the mechanism has been replicated for decades and outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease are cited, so none treats it as premature.
Members agree the main weakness of B025 is attribution (contested priority for the active peptide, Habener outside the credited names, Knudsen left out), not science or maturity.

Four members (El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg) and the chair name B045 (Mori and Walter) as an alternative or as the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, and no one disputes the stability of the UPR mechanism.
Members agree that B050 (optogenetics) is held back by a six-name allocation problem under the three-person limit, whatever its impact.
scientific_disputes: Whether B045 should be weighed on its disease relevance and translation. Linnarsson and Wahren-Herlenius see developing clinical payoff (Wahren-Herlenius also notes that the PERK and ATF6 branches complicate a Walter and Mori pair), while Perlmann, Sandberg and the chair argue that a new organelle-to-nucleus signalling logic is the kind of conceptual change the prize rewards.

Whether B050 is a discovery or a tool. El Manira, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius and the chair raise the discovery-versus-method question, and Wahren-Herlenius notes that methods have been honoured before. Linnarsson also doubts a tool is as strong a case as a mechanism or therapy.

Whether B031 (TNF blockade) is a new discovery of principle or translation of earlier cytokine biology. Wahren-Herlenius ranks it second and calls it a paradigm shift, while El Manira, Perlmann, Linnarsson and Sandberg read it as clinical proof of concept. Wahren-Herlenius lists it as an alternative.

Relative strength of B051 (CAR-T) against B045: Sandberg and the chair describe CAR-T as the stronger clinical case (approved products, durable remissions) but with open questions on solid tumours and toxicity, while B045 is cleaner and more conceptual.
attribution_disputes: B025: priority for identifying and synthesising the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is contested, and Habener cannot be added because he is outside the credited names. Members differ on whether this argues for careful citation wording (Sandberg, El Manira, Wahren-Herlenius) or for examining the priority evidence before the final ballot (chair, Perlmann).

B025: Mojsov versus Knudsen for the third place. Linnarsson's opening trio was Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, and the others opening with Mojsov regard Knudsen's acylated analogues as industrial drug development, while acknowledging that they are why the discovery reached patients. The committee has not established whether the citation should reward the physiology or the therapeutic step.

B051: Eshhar is outside the credited names. Perlmann treats this as more than a caveat, since the conceptual origin, costimulation design and clinical proof are separate achievements, and notes that Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy is a different line of work. Sandberg treats it as a caveat, El Manira lists the missing Eshhar credit as an uncertainty, and the chair calls the attribution incomplete.

B050: six credited names for at most three places. In the opening ballots all six members proposed trios drawn from Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, which omit Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck. Wahren-Herlenius separates the channelrhodopsin characterisation (Bamberg, Nagel, Hegemann) from the neuronal demonstration (Boyden, Deisseroth), and notes Miesenboeck's earlier work bears on priority.

B001: Hall is the clear core, but the mammalian target credit is spread across several groups. Perlmann and Sandberg prefer a Hall-centred award, the chair doubts a Sabatini and Schreiber trio is as defensible as B045, and Linnarsson disputes the claim that it is cleaner than GLP-1.
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B025, B031 or B045.
B051: durable remissions and approved products are accepted, but solid-tumour efficacy and toxicity remain open (chair, Wahren-Herlenius), and Wahren-Herlenius contrasts it with the more mature B031.

B045: members differ on whether the still-developing disease translation is a reason for patience (chair), a limit on its rank (Linnarsson, Wahren-Herlenius), or an irrelevant test for a conceptual discovery (Perlmann, Sandberg).
Wahren-Herlenius notes that the commercial success of the GLP-1 field may overshadow the underlying science; no one else raises this as a maturity point.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member reports a conflict with any credited name on the shortlist, and no recusal is requested.
El Manira discloses co-authorship with Perlmann (2009), Grillner (2019 review) and Ernfors; none is a credited name.
Linnarsson discloses a connection to the 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper and to co-authors including Sandberg; none is a credited name.
Perlmann discloses connections to Ronald Evans and Johan Ericson, and co-authorship with the chair and El Manira; none is a credited name.
Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and with Jonas Frisen; none is a credited name.

The chair discloses a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard and co-authorship with Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy; neither concerns a credited name. Wahren-Herlenius declares none, noting her rheumatology field and that Feldmann and Maini work on rheumatoid arthritis, but documents no tie to them.

El Manira flags that his motor-circuit field is relevant only to B050, which he treats on the common criteria. The chair also states familiarity with circuit methods and says it should not raise B050 in his ranking.
questions_for_round2: For B025, does the evidence supplied support Mojsov's priority for identifying and synthesising the active peptide over Habener and others, and how should the citation word a contested priority?
For B025, should the citation reward the physiology and peptide identification only, or the therapeutic step, and if the latter, which of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov would give up a place to Knudsen?
If B025 occupies all three places, does any member support a second achievement sharing the prize, which would require removing a GLP-1 name, or should round 2 treat B025 as a stand-alone award?
If the committee wants a second option behind B025, which of B045, B051 or B031 is preferred, and is the cleaner attribution of B045 worth more than the clinical evidence of B051 and B031?
For B051, does the absence of Eshhar make the June, Sadelain and Rosenberg configuration unworkable, or is it a caveat that citation wording can address?
For B050, is there any defensible three-name allocation among Bamberg, Nagel, Hegemann, Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenboeck, and is a method award within the category?
For B031, does Wahren-Herlenius see the cytokine biology credit as covered by Feldmann and Maini, as Linnarsson asked, and does that change the views of those who read it as translation?
summary.chair_observation: The six round-1 files agree on one configuration, B025 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and no member expresses a competing first preference, but unanimity on the ballot is not unanimity on attribution: each statement carries the same open questions on Mojsov, Habener and Knudsen. Alternatives are B045 (four members and the chair), B051 (all six members), B031 (Wahren-Herlenius only) and none of B001, B050, B018, B046 or B010, so round 2 should test the GLP-1 attribution evidence before it explores second options.
